question: I have a gene expression matrix in CSV format. Generate a clustered heatmap using row-wise Z-score normalization and default hierarchical clustering. Label samples and genes clearly.

files.eval_guideline: Heatmap must show row Z-score coloring with hierarchical clustering dendrograms on both axes and labeled genes and samples; color palette and font size may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical name clustered_heatmap.png and PNG image format, matching the requested clustered gene expression heatmap. The other candidate, answer.md, is a Markdown document rather than the requested image.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires visual confirmation of row-wise Z-score coloring, hierarchical clustering dendrograms on both axes, and clearly labeled genes and samples. Semantic comparison evaluates these features while allowing differences in palette and font size.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show a clustered heatmap of 100 genes across 20 samples, with row-wise Z-score coloring, hierarchical clustering dendrograms on both axes, and labeled genes and samples. The sample ordering matches, including the clear separation of Samples 1–10 from Samples 11–20. Gene ordering and distinctive cell patterns also visually match, supporting that the same normalized data and clustering are represented. Both convey predominantly lower relative expression in the left sample cluster and higher relative expression in the right cluster. Each includes a diverging blue–white–red scale centered at zero. The candidate explicitly identifies average linkage and Euclidean distance in its title. Differences in palette saturation, colorbar orientation, plot proportions, gridlines, and label sizing are cosmetic; the candidate's taller layout improves gene-label readability. No scientifically important elements appear missing.
